name: Banff Skatepark
why: A New Line Skateparks build off Sundance Road beside the town's ball diamonds, with a long snake-run bowl (hips, extensions, vert walls, pump bumps) and a street course of hubbas, stairs, handrails, a pole jam and a Euro gap.
heads_up: Open sunrise to sunset; watch for fly balls from the ball diamonds next door and give elk and other wildlife plenty of space.

name: Callingwood Skatepark
why: A 19,500 sq ft New Line Skateparks street park in west Edmonton with granite-topped hubba ledges, stair sets, handrails, gaps, manual pads and a half pipe.
heads_up: Listed hours are sunrise to sunset; it's mostly street terrain, so transition skaters may want to pair it with Castle Downs or Mill Woods.

name: Castle Downs Skatepark
why: A large all-concrete park on 153 Avenue NW beside the Castle Downs YMCA, with a big flow bowl (hips, extension, roller, roll-in and a transfer spine) and a full street course.
heads_up: Open 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.; Edmonton asks skaters to ride only when the surface is dry and free of snow and ice.

name: Cowboys Park Skatepark (formerly Shaw Millennium Park)
why: Opened in 2000 on the west edge of downtown, its 75,000 sq ft of concrete is Canada's largest outdoor skatepark, with street, intermediate and advanced courses, a cloverleaf bowl and a large full pipe. Locals still call it 'Millz' after the Shaw Millennium Park name, which changed to Cowboys Park in 2024.
heads_up: The skatepark is open 24 hours, but some bowls close for the Cowboys Music Festival around Stampede (roughly mid-June to mid-July).

name: Fairview Bike Pump Track
why: Calgary's first asphalt pump track, built in 2020 by Bike Track for the Fairview Community Association, with small tabletops and beginner, intermediate and advanced routes.
heads_up: Parking is limited; don't park in the alley behind Fairview Drive. Open 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

name: Genesis Centre Skatepark
why: Northeast Calgary's first official skatepark, built by New Line Skateparks in front of the Genesis Centre in Martindale and opened in 2019, with a large bowl and a mostly street layout of hubbas, ledges, rails and stairs.
heads_up: Listed as open 24/7; it sits in front of the Genesis Centre on Falconridge Blvd NE.

name: Glendale Skatepark
why: A New Line Skateparks park of almost 18,000 sq ft with a pool-style bowl, a large flow bowl and street terrain of hubbas, handrails, stair sets, an A-frame ledge and a pole jam, a natural stop on the drive between Edmonton and Calgary.
heads_up: Lit and listed as open 24/7.

name: Huntington Hills Skatepark
why: One of the first three parks built in 2015 under Calgary's skatepark strategy, with a large bowl of extensions, hips, a spine and a pool-style pocket with pool coping, plus hubbas, a handrail, stairs and manual pads.
heads_up: A neighbourhood park at Centre St N and 64 Ave NW, so keep the noise down for the neighbours late in the day.

name: Inglewood Bike Pump Track
why: Opened in October 2021 at 2040 7 Ave S.E., designed by Ground Cubed and Velosolutions: two asphalt tracks for beginner and intermediate riders, just off the Bow River pathway.
heads_up: Free drop-in, 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

name: Inland Skatepark
why: In Kin Coulee Park below Medicine Hat College, where a 13,500 sq ft addition in 2013 added an upper bowl, a hubba with two rails, and a plaza with a brick bank-to-ledge, a big three-stair, a gap and a warped 'sushi dish' manual pad.
heads_up: It's down the hill from the college on Kipling Street; the older park's terrain sits alongside the 2013 addition.

name: Mill Woods Skatepark
why: One of Edmonton's older parks, by the Mill Woods Recreation Centre, with a bowl of hips, volcanoes and pump bumps and a brick China bank, plus ledges, rails, a Euro gap and a bank-to-bank gap.
heads_up: It's lit and open 24/7, but the older concrete has big cracks, so watch your wheels.

name: New Brighton Skatepark
why: A New Line Skateparks build in southeast Calgary whose bowl has several hips, pocket and vert extensions and a roll-in, next to a street section with two stair sets with handrails, out ledges and a long flat bar.
heads_up: Check the bowl is dry and clear of gravel before dropping in after a storm.

name: South Glenmore Bike Pump Track
why: Velosolutions built two connected asphalt tracks here in 2020, a 110 m beginner loop and a 204 m loop with bigger features, raised above ground because of the high water table by the Glenmore Reservoir.
heads_up: Open 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.; park at 3520 90 Ave S.W. and ride east on the Elbow River pathway.

name: Southwood Skatepark
why: Another of Calgary's 2015 strategy parks, set in a quiet southwest neighbourhood park, with a flow bowl of varying depths and a radial pocket plus ledges, rails, stairs and a bank with an inset ledge.
heads_up: Listed hours are 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.; it's a residential area, so keep it respectful.

name: The Compound Indoor Skatepark
why: Calgary's only indoor skatepark by its own account, run by the Riders on Board snowboard club in a 20,000 sq ft warehouse with a street section, a large mini bowl, flat-ground courts and a beginner area with a 2 ft micro mini.
heads_up: A helmet and a signed waiver are mandatory, and public drop-in runs on set hours, so check the schedule first.

name: West Confederation Bike Pump Track
why: Calgary's newest Velosolutions track, in the southeast corner of West Confederation Park, with a 90 m intermediate loop and a 145 m advanced loop of five berms each.
heads_up: Groups can book it on weekdays; outside bookings it is open for drop-in, 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

name: Woodlands Skatepark
why: Rebuilt on the old park's site in Legion Memorial Park in 2020, this 14,000 sq ft park has a 5–8 ft pool-style bowl, a 4 ft mini-ramp bowl, a flow bowl with a banked spine and centre island, and a street area.
heads_up: Lights stay on until 11 p.m.; the fenced park's only entrance is on the northeast side, behind the kids' water park.

name: Chilliwack Pump Track
why: Velosolutions built two asphalt tracks at The Landing in late 2020: a pro track of over 300 m with a tunnel, which Velosolutions calls the only one of its kind in North America, and a shorter intermediate track.
heads_up: The pro track is fast and can intimidate young riders; start on the smaller track. Turf edges give softer landings.

name: China Creek Skatepark
why: Vancouver's first skatepark, opened in May 1979 on a filled-in ravine after local skaters worked with a neighbourhood committee on the design. The Vancouver Heritage Foundation named it a Place That Matters in 2022, and the Park Board has been renewing it.
heads_up: No lights, so it's a daylight session; BMX riders share the bowls, so take turns.

name: Chuck Bailey Skatepark
why: About 30,000 sq ft of concrete outside the Chuck Bailey Recreation Centre, mixing a large plaza of ramps, rails and bowls with local art, plus a 5,000 sq ft covered bowl area built for wet-weather riding.
heads_up: Only the covered bowl area stays dry in the rain; the rest of the plaza is open to the weather.

name: Garden City Bike Park
why: Richmond's bike park on Granville Avenue has an obstacle section with skinnies and a teeter-totter, and a dirt jump area with jumps laid out by skill level, from beginner to expert.
heads_up: Dirt jumps: let them dry out after rain.

name: Hastings Park Bike Skills Track
why: In the southeast corner of Hastings Park at the north end of Empire Field: a dirt pump track with sculpted berms, a smaller pump track for kids and wooden skills platforms and ramps.
heads_up: Gets busy in late afternoons; dirt sections need to dry after rain.

name: Hastings Skateboard Park
why: A big concrete park on the west side of Hastings Park, between the PNE Forum and the Italian Gardens, with three connected bowls (the deep end runs about 11 feet) and a small street area. It has hosted contests including the Vans Park Series.
heads_up: Street parking around the PNE grounds is restricted, so use PNE parking; the bowls fill up on dry summer evenings.

name: Inter River Bike Park
why: Opened in 2019 beside a former BMX park, with a BMX dirt jump course, a paved pump track and a dirt pump track. Landyachtz has held timed skateboard races on the paved loop.
heads_up: The jump course is for experienced riders; beginners and intermediates should stick to the pump tracks.

name: Jordie Lunn Bike Park
why: Velosolutions built a 1,500 m² main pump track, a kids' track and a roughly 142 m downhill snake run here in 2020 on a steep site that honours rider Jordie Lunn; the park also has jump and skills zones.
heads_up: The pump tracks have no lights, so plan to ride in daylight.

name: Kamloops Bike Ranch
why: Set up in 2005 inside city limits, the Ranch has jump lines like Tombstone and Wrangler, the floodlit Corral dirt jumps, a BMX track and a new $1.3 million all-wheels pump track.
heads_up: Dirt lines need to dry after rain; a local shuttle (Mostly Mental Shuttles) has run laps to the top.

name: Kensington Skateboard Park
why: A compact East Vancouver park at Knight Street and East 37th Avenue built around a pool-style bowl about 9.5 feet at the deep end and 5 feet at the shallow end, plus a mini-ramp and amphitheatre-style ledges.
heads_up: No lights; the pool bowl is deep for a small park, so newer skaters should warm up on the mini-ramp.

name: Leeside Tunnel Skateboard Park
why: A volunteer-built DIY park inside an abandoned 49 m tunnel under the Cassiar Connector at East Hastings, named for skater and artist Lee Matasi, who was killed in Gastown in 2005. About a dozen hand-built mini-ramps, quarter pipes and grind poles fill the tunnel.
heads_up: Reach it down the lane behind the E-Comm building off East Pender; laneway parking is tight, so park on East Pender and keep the driveways clear.

name: Metro Skate Park (Bonsor Park)
why: Next to Metrotown in Bonsor Park, with a street zone, a bowl zone that includes a full pipe, and a beginner section with a shallow bowl and grind curbs.
heads_up: No lights, so plan a daylight session; beginners have their own shallow-bowl section away from the full pipe.

name: Mountain Air Bike Skills Park
why: Built for mountain bikers on the north side of Burnaby Mountain, with skinnies, elevated bridges, drops, teeter-totters, wood and dirt pump tracks and dirt jumps.
heads_up: Washrooms and picnic tables on site; wooden features get slick in the wet.

name: One Love Indoor Skatepark
why: A non-profit indoor park that opened in October 2021 in a former grocery store in Whalley, run by the faith-based One Love International Society and led by former pro skater Dan Pageau, with wooden ramps, lessons and a skate shop.
heads_up: The wooden ramps get moved around for Sunday services, so the layout and hours change; check before you go.

name: Pemberton Bike Skills Park
why: Opened in 2022 in Den Duyf Park with four zones (pump track, skills park, drop zone and jump lines) rated so riders can progress. It was paid for mostly by a provincial grant of about $974,000.
heads_up: Closed 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. (until 9 a.m. on Sundays and holidays).

name: Penticton Youthpark
why: In Riverside Park at the west end of the beach, with a very large street section of ledges, hubbas, rails, banks, quarter pipes and stair sets alongside a large flow bowl.
heads_up: It's beside a go-kart track and bumper boats, so summer days are busy; public washrooms are nearby and there's a large lot to the north.

name: Penzer Bike Park
why: Part of Penzer Action Park: a BMX-style dirt jump area (2008) and a cement pump track (2017), next to a skatepark, a parkour area and an in-ground trampoline.
heads_up: The pump track is shared with skateboards and scooters, so watch the traffic at busy times.

name: Railside Skate Park
why: At the south end of Lions Park beside the rail yards, mixing a street area of rails, hips, stairs and ledges with a large bowl zone.
heads_up: It sits right beside an active rail yard, so keep clear of the tracks; there's no cover when it rains.

name: Seylynn Bowl
why: A concrete snake run that drops into a bowl, first ridden in 1978 and known as Canada's oldest surviving skatepark. Monty Little, who later designed the original Whistler park, co-designed it.
heads_up: The concrete is decades old with patches and cracks, so walk your line first; it's tucked behind trees by the ball diamonds on Hunter Street, open dawn to dusk.

name: Sicamous Pump Track
why: Asphalt pump track in Finlayson Park that hosted the first UCI Pump Track World Championships Canada Qualifier in 2024, with nearly 50 riders, and the qualifier again in 2025.
heads_up: It sits beside the skatepark and rec centre in Finlayson Park, so it pairs well with a skate session.

name: Sidney Skatepark
why: In Tulista Park about 25 km north of downtown Victoria, pairing a bowl of varied depths with an extension and pocket with a full street section of stairs, a hubba, a handrail, a brick bank and a camel hump.
heads_up: Listed hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.

name: Silver Star Bike Park
why: Lift-served park at Silver Star Mountain Resort above Vernon. When the Georgia Straight covered it in 2013 it had 18 trails over 44 km, including the 7 km Paradise Trail for beginners.
heads_up: Trail figures are from 2013; check the resort for current lift days and tickets.

name: SORCA Bike Skills Park
why: Rebuilt by the Squamish Off-Road Cycling Association next to the Brennan Park Recreation Centre (the original park dates from 2014), with three jump lines (green, blue and double blue), a paved pump track, drops and skinnies.
heads_up: Free to ride; SORCA asks riders to buy an optional yearly trail pass (sold at Corsa Cycles) to pay for upkeep.

name: Squamish BMX Track
why: Refreshed BMX track between Brennan Park and Kinsmen Campground with straights, berm turns, rollers, rhythm sections and tabletops, a short walk from the SORCA skills park.
heads_up: Dirt track: give it time to dry after rain.

name: Stevie Smith Bike Park
why: Velosolutions built a beginner track and a larger competition track here in 2017. The park hosts Red Bull Pump Track World Championship qualifiers, including the only Canadian stop in 2018.
heads_up: The competition track is for confident riders; warm up on the beginner loop.

name: Sun Peaks Bike Park
why: Lift-served park at Sun Peaks Resort near Kamloops, running since 1999, with more than 89 km of trails and 595 m of vertical. It grew onto Sundance Mountain in 2022 and hosts the Canadian National Downhill Championships.
heads_up: Seasonal: the 2026 season ran June 13 to September 27; lift ticket required.

name: Topaz Skatepark
why: A 3,000 m² all-wheels park built by New Line Skateparks that opened in August 2022 in Topaz Park, with a big bowl stepping from 6- and 8-foot pool-block sections to a 10-foot section with steel coping, a street line along the path and smaller beginner features.
heads_up: Floodlights switch off in sequence at 10 p.m. to signal closing; a bike pump track sits next door, so watch for riders.

name: UBC Skatepark
why: Billed as North America's first on-campus concrete skatepark, it packs a bowled mini-ramp, ledges, rails and a ledge shaped like a stack of books into a compact spot on Thunderbird Boulevard.
heads_up: Small footprint, so watch for skaters crossing your line; there's no cover from rain.

name: Vancouver Skate Plaza (Downtown Skateboard Plaza)
why: A 2,000 m² street plaza under the Georgia and Dunsmuir viaducts, opened in 2004 and upgraded in 2011, with replica rails, embankments, curbs, walls and steps in granite, brick, concrete and steel. Complex magazine ranked it #21 on its 2013 list of the world's best skateparks.
heads_up: The viaducts overhead keep most of it dry in the rain, but the city has long planned to remove them and replace the plaza, so check the city page before a trip.

name: Vanier Park Bike Skills Track
why: Built in 2010 and kept up by volunteers, it sits in the trees on the south side of Vanier Park by the Burrard Street Bridge, with dirt jumps of several sizes and two pump tracks, the smaller one for kids.
heads_up: All dirt and no lights: ride in daylight and skip it after heavy rain.

name: Vic West Skatepark
why: Victoria's long-running park at 250 Esquimalt Road, a New Line Skateparks project first built in 2002 with a second phase in 2017, with one fully enclosed bowl, one open flow bowl and modern street terrain.
heads_up: The enclosed bowl has steel and pool coping, so wear a helmet; there's no roof, so let it dry after a shower.

name: Whistler Mountain Bike Park
why: Lift-served park on Whistler Mountain, open since 1999, with over 900 vertical metres of terrain reached by chairlift and gondola. It has hosted Crankworx events, including a pump track challenge at the Boneyard in 2010.
heads_up: Summer lift ticket required; check Whistler Blackcomb for this season's opening and closing dates.

name: Whistler Skatepark
why: Designed by Monty Little and built with Terry Snyder, it opened to skaters in August 1990 with a snake run into a 6.5 m-wide 'Snake Bowl'. Later phases driven by local skaters (the third opened in 2016) grew it past 50,000 sq ft, which the municipality counts as Canada's second-largest skatepark.
heads_up: Open April to November; the lights run until 1 a.m. on a push-button timer, helmets are recommended and mountain bikes aren't allowed. Access is through Day Lot 3.

name: Píhtikwé Skatepark
why: A community-run indoor park whose name is Cree for 'come in'; it opened in Portage Place in fall 2023 and reopened in October 2026 at 323 Portage Avenue, across from Canada Life Centre, with loaner boards, lessons and family sessions.
heads_up: Drop-in sessions run Thursday to Saturday; youth $3, adults $10 and free for Indigenous skaters, and staff will help anyone who can't pay. Check the site for current times.

name: The Plaza at The Forks
why: Opened in 2006 at The Forks, about 44,000 sq ft of plaza with rails, ledges, banks, steps and skateable art such as the steel 'magic carpet', plus an 8,500 sq ft bowl. Designed by van der Zalm + Associates and New Line Skateparks, it was Canada's most expensive skatepark when built ($2.5 million).
heads_up: It's a busy public site, so watch for people walking through the plaza on summer evenings.

name: Bayview Arena Bike Park
why: A 3,000 m² dirt park behind Bayview Arena in North York with jumps, berms and tabletops for a range of skill levels.
heads_up: Open dawn to dusk; park at the arena. Let the dirt dry after rain.

name: Carlington Bike Park
why: Led by the Ottawa Mountain Bike Association with the City of Ottawa, it sits on the former ski hill in Carlington Park, with three granite-surface circuits for beginner to advanced riders.
heads_up: Easy to reach by bus and bike path, so you don't need a car.

name: Centennial Park Pan Am BMX Centre
why: The BMX venue of the Toronto 2015 Pan Am Games: a compact closed-loop course with four straights, three banked turns, 5 m and 8 m start ramps and several challenging jumps.
heads_up: Open dawn to dusk from May 2 to October 31, weather permitting.

name: Joyride 150
why: Indoor bike park that opened in December 2009 in a building of over 100,000 sq ft, with beginner to expert sections, a foam pit and resi jump, jump and rhythm lines, a BMX street park, a pump track and an indoor cross-country loop.
heads_up: Paid day passes (about $31 for ages 7 and up, less after 7 p.m.); bring your own bike and helmet or rent them there.

name: Kivi Park Pump Track
why: A newer intermediate dirt pump track with banked turns and rollers at Kivi Park, which has more than 55 km of trails.
heads_up: Kivi Park charges a day pass ($9, family $25, kids 10 and under free); bike rentals from $25 for 2 hours.

name: Phil Esposito Park Pump Track
why: One of the first asphalt pump tracks in Ontario, with beginner rollers and banked turns plus an advanced 'butterfly' route, linked to more than 30 km of mountain bike trails.
heads_up: Bike rentals are available in town for about $50 a day.

name: Sunnyside Bike Park
why: Opened in 2014 about 150 m from Lake Ontario, partly from recycled materials, with pump tracks, a skills trail, a large drop, a boardwalk and a wall ride, rated green to black.
heads_up: Open dawn to dusk; no parking on site, only a drop-off roundabout at Lake Shore Blvd. W. and Ellis Ave.

name: Camp Fortune Pump Track
why: Camp Fortune's pump track sits on NCC land in Gatineau Park. A 2023 federal assessment covered a 215 m expansion with a start ramp, two berms, five tabletops and six rollers, the first phase of a mountain bike skills park.
heads_up: It is built on native soil, so wait for it to dry after rain.

name: Empire 47 Pump Track
why: At 1,800 m² it is the largest pump track in the Quebec City area. The Velosolutions-built track has hosted a Red Bull UCI Pump Track World Championships qualifier and is lit in the evening.
heads_up: Paid access (adult day pass about $24), and the park closes on rainy days.

name: Runway Bike Park
why: Velosolutions designed the asphalt pump track at The Jones Center: about 25,000 sq ft. It opened in fall 2018 and that October hosted the first Red Bull Pump Track World Championship final. The 2.75-acre park also has three asphalt skills lines with cedar and steel features, and a bicycle playground for small kids.
heads_up: The Jones Center lends out bikes and helmets for free, so you can ride without bringing your own.

name: Truckee Bike Park
why: Three flow lines (beginner, intermediate and advanced) that you drop into and pump over berms and jumps, plus a side-by-side Dual Pump track and a start-to-finish Straight Rhythm line.
heads_up: Truckee is snow country, so expect a winter off-season; check conditions before you drive up.

name: Griffin Bike Park
why: A 300-acre bike park with more than two dozen lines. They run from the one-mile, all-ability Basic Training Skills Loop of berms and hips to Mega Pump, an expert 0.6-mile pump trail with three big jumps.
heads_up: OpenStreetMap lists it as open 24/7 "weather permitting", so check conditions after rain.

name: Keene Creek Bike Park
why: Built by volunteers with COGGS (Cyclists of Gitchee Gumee Shores) on about an acre near and partly under Interstate 35. It has a dirt jump plaza with beginner, intermediate and advanced lines, a pump track, and a bike playground of wooden features.
heads_up: Parts of the park are still being built; the city lists the beginner, intermediate and advanced jump lines as open.

name: Kinetic Park
why: This St. Charles County park, formerly the Youth Activity Park, has what the county billed as the largest asphalt pump track in the nation. It hosted Red Bull UCI Pump Track World Championships qualifiers in 2021 and 2022.
heads_up: OpenStreetMap lists the park as open 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily; check St. Charles County Parks for current hours.

name: MOmentum Bike Park
why: A new city bike park in its first season in 2026. Joplin is one of four US communities hosting a 2026 Velosolutions/UCI Pump Track qualifier, held at the park on August 15–16, 2026.
heads_up: OpenStreetMap lists it as open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; the park is brand new, so check with the City of Joplin for current details.

name: George Poston Park Pump Track
why: North Carolina's first Velosolutions pump track, about 10,000 sq ft, in a Gaston County park that also has more than 10 miles of singletrack. It hosted Red Bull UCI Pump Track World Championships qualifiers, including in 2021 and 2022.
heads_up: The coordinates mark the park as a whole; the pump track is one part of a larger park with trails.

name: Dayton Bike Yard
why: A newer bike park in Welcome Park with about 2.5 acres of jumps, a pump track, and areas set aside for beginners and families.
heads_up: The coordinates mark the pump track; the jump areas fill the rest of the 2.5-acre site.

name: Mike's Bike Park
why: Two floors of indoor riding in a former downtown radiator factory, opened in 2016 by Mike Bisig. It has a pump track, jumps, ramps, skinnies, a foam pit, a cross-country loop and a beginner section, and almost anything without a motor is allowed.
heads_up: Open year-round; everyone signs a waiver before riding.

name: Ray's MTB Indoor Park
why: Opened in 2004 in a former factory on Cleveland's west side and since grown to about 165,000 sq ft. It has a full-size indoor pump track, a jump trail, foam pits, a BMX pool, and a trail of nearly a mile with rocks and logs built to feel like the woods.
heads_up: Seasonal: usually open October to April and closed in summer; riders under 18 need a waiver signed by a parent.

name: Piney Mountain Bike Lounge
why: A mellow pump track of rollers and berms at a bike lounge with beer and food trucks. It is lit, so riding carries on after dark, and staff are on hand to give tips.
heads_up: The lights stay on only while the lounge is open and staffed, so riding follows its hours.

name: Paris Pump Track
why: An asphalt pump track on the Trail de Paris that hosted Red Bull UCI Pump Track World Championships qualifiers in May 2021 and July 2022.
heads_up: OpenStreetMap says it has no lights, so it's a daylight ride.

name: I-5 Colonnade Mountain Bike Park
why: Seattle's urban mountain bike park in I-5 Colonnade Park, under the freeway. Seattle Parks and the Evergreen Mountain Bike Alliance planned to rebuild its Tqalu Skills Zone with two paved pump tracks.
heads_up: The paved pump tracks were set for construction in summer–fall 2024; check Seattle Parks to see whether they have opened.

name: Leavenworth Pump Track
why: An asphalt pump track built by Velosolutions that hosted Red Bull Pump Track World Championship qualifiers in 2018 and 2019.
heads_up: OpenStreetMap says it has no lights, so plan to ride in daylight.
